To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the management of sepses and septic shock should be based upon a systematic approach that includes early goal directed resuscitation, the early administration of antibiotics, and the use of vasopressors to support a mean arterial pressure of greater than 65 mm Hg.

(1) early goal directed therapy is effective for the initial treatment of sepsis; (2) early broad spectrum antimicrobial therapy is effective for sepsis, but not septic shock, in adults and children; (3) steroids are not recommended for sepsis and should not be used in septic shock; (4) activated protein C is effective in adult septic shock but is not recommended for pediatric use; (5) the use of recombinant human activated protein
early goal directed therapy is the best way to improve outcome of patients with sepsis.
